Maya: Kicking off the EU-CENTRAL GPU pool bring-up. Target: 24xA100 nodes, baseline SLOs and handoff tonight. Will run a short smoke + acceptance pass.
Sam: 👍 What's our quick checklist for smoke?
Maya: Short list — node provisioning, GPU visibility, network egress, control-plane API, sample inference latency, and a basic load run (burst 50 qps). Also cost sanity check on spot vs reserved.
Ben: I'll take node provisioning + GPU checks. Plan: provision node pool, verify `nvidia-smi` and driver versions, then run a simple CUDA microbench.
Ashley: I'll own networking and control-plane. I'll validate VPC peering, firewall rules, and routing to CI runners.
Eli: I'll run the inference smoke and SLO gating. Quick script: `./smoke/inference_smoke.sh --model test-small --qps 50 --duration 60`
Ops-Bot: [deploy-bot] Provision job started for pool `eu-central1-gpu-24`. Job id: job-20260318-001
Ben: Node provisioning done. 24 nodes in GKE pool `gpu-prod-euc`. Drivers: NVIDIA 525.85.12, CUDA 11.8. Quick GPU check:
```
$ kubectl -n infra run gpu-check --image=nvidia/cuda:11.8-base --restart=Never --rm -it -- nvidia-smi -L
GPU 0: A100-SXM4 (UUID: GPU-xxxx)
...
```
Ben: Also ran a short throughput microbench: 126 GB/s bandwidth nominal, no ECC errors.
Ashley: Networking checks: BGP sessions to the egress gateway established, VPC peering with infra-prod confirmed. Firewall rules allow 443/9443 from control plane CIDR. CI runners can reach the service IPs.
Maya: Great. Now ops SLO acceptance: we require p95 < 220ms for the test-small model at 50 qps and error rate < 0.5% for the run. Eli, run the smoke and capture metrics.
Eli: Running smoke now. Command and quick log:
```
$ ./smoke/inference_smoke.sh --model test-small --qps 50 --duration 60 --target http://eu-central1.redwood.internal/generate
Starting run: 60s @ 50qps
Requests: 3000, Errors: 6, p50=90ms, p95=210ms, p99=380ms
```
Eli: Results look within SLOs: p95=210ms < 220ms, error rate = 0.2%. No timeouts.
Maya: Cost sanity check? What does the quick estimate look like for reserved vs spot? Ben: Rough calc: reserved monthly ~ $13k, spot avg utilization for bursty < $6.5k but no SLA. For Dedicated customers we'll recommend reserved.
Ashley: Also validated autoscaler behavior: scale-up from 24->30 under synthetic load worked, nodes joined and pods scheduled within 90s.
Sam: Any remaining failures or surprises in logs? Share a snippet if so.
Eli: One odd 500 in run with model shard error, traced to a cold-start kernel compile event — happened once, nothing reproducible. Logging entry: `runtime: kernel-compile-timeout=120s -> success after retry`
Maya: Noted. We'll add a workflow step to warm key kernels post-deploy.
Ops-Bot: [ops] Canary traffic policy applied: 10% to eu-central1 pool for 1h, fallback route ready to `eu-west1` in case p95 breaches 300ms.
Ben: Handoff checklist for SRE: 1) Terraform state in infra-terraform (PR merged). 2) K8s secrets rotated via vault (done). 3) Alerting: p99 > 500ms, error rate >1%, node GPU memory pressure > 85% — all defined. 4) Runbook link: /runbooks/eu-central1-gpu-ops (will push doc).
Ashley: Added a temporary network egress cost alert for the first 24 hours (threshold $1k/day).
Maya: Final pre-handoff notes: schedule a 30m readiness review at 21:30 UTC, include oncall and platform-eng. If all good, we flip production traffic to include eu-central1 100% within 6h window.
Sam: Sounds good. I'm available for the review. :thumbsup:
Eli: I'll monitor dashboards and post a 15m update.
Ops-Bot: [deploy-bot] Canary rollout completed to 10% with healthy metrics.
Maya: Excellent work team — if no objections, we'll proceed to full handoff after the readiness review.
Ben: No objections.
Ashley: No objections.
Eli: No objections.
Maya: OK closing this thread and tracking the review meeting notes in calendar invite. Thanks all. :rocket:
